subject: Results of GoF sensitive to number of occasions

messages.author: 4e49888ed5efaf4f
messages.subject: Results of GoF sensitive to number of occasions
parts:
Hello unmarked Google group,

This is my first post as I am new to the group!

I am studying the distribution of coyotes in the Sonoran desert. Due to high naïve occupancy, I am using the Royle-Nichols model. My camera trap dataset corresponds to a single season of 82 trapping nights for 87 sites, resulting in 533 coyote captures.

I first ran the analysis keeping the 82 occasions. My global model has 7 covariates, which complies with the rule of one covariate per 30 captures: 
occuRN(~effort + occ ~NDVI + Palm + Wat + SF + BTJ, CYT)

I then ran a MacKenzie & Bailey Goodness of fit test calling for: 
mb.gof.test(RN.CYT_global2, nsim = 1000, plot.hist = TRUE, maxK = NULL). 

The P-value (0.443) is fine, but the c-hat is very low (0.19392). Looking at the chi-square table, I noticed that most of the expected frequencies were pretty low, resulting in large chi-square values. The same phenomenon seemed to happen with simulated data sets, with wide quantile intervals.

Following recommendations found in group conversations, I then ran the model pooling 3 and 7 trapping nights together. On average, observed and expected frequencies increased, leading to lower values of chi-square. However, P-value and c-hat are very sensitive to pooling:

·        3 trapping nights: P-value = 0.071, c-hat = 1.83631

·        7 trapping nights: P-value = 0.826, c-hat = 0.69597

Has anyone encountered this issue? If I want to keep 82 occasions to get the maximum number of detections, would it be possible to use an alternative test to estimate P-value and c-hat? For instance, the Freeman-Tukey test (sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2) quoted in the unmarked manual?

Thank you in advance for your help!

Marie
